title: React Context
description: Learn how to share data across components without prop drilling.

data.text: **Context** provides a way to pass data through the component tree without manually threading props through every intermediate level. It solves the **prop drilling** problem cleanly.
When a deeply nested child needs data from a top-level parent, you must pass that data through every component in between — even if those intermediate components do not use it.

data.title: Prop Drilling
data.content: Passing props through components that don't need them

data.text: Create a context object with `createContext()`. Wrap your tree with a Provider that supplies the value. Any descendant can then read that value.

data.title: Create and Provide Context
Don't Overuse Context
data.text: Context is great for truly global data. For component-specific communication, props are simpler. Overusing context makes components harder to reuse and test.
The value passed to `createContext` is a fallback used only when a component reads the context outside a Provider. Always provide a sensible default.

data.title: Default Value
data.content: Using a default value in createContext

data.text: You can nest multiple Providers. Components consume whichever contexts they need. For complex apps, consider splitting contexts by concern (theme, auth, locale) rather than one mega-context.

data.caption: Context flows from Provider to any descendant, skipping intermediate components.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Provider] --> B[Intermediate Component]
    B --> C[Intermediate Component]
    C --> D[Consumer]
    A -.->|context skips B & C| D

terms.definition: A mechanism for passing data through the component tree without prop drilling.
A component that accepts a value prop and makes it available to descendants.
Passing props through components that do not need them.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Theme Context
data.description: Create a theme context and consume it in deeply nested components.
steps: Wrap the app with ThemeProvider that holds a theme state.
Create a deeply nested Button component that reads the theme from context.
Add a toggle in the header that updates the theme.
data.expectedOutcome: A theme toggle that updates the entire app without prop drilling.

items.question: How many contexts should I create?
items.answer: Create one per concern. Separate theme, auth, and locale into different contexts. One mega-context causes unnecessary re-renders.

items.question: Does Context replace Redux?
items.answer: For simple global state, yes. For complex state with time-travel debugging, middleware, or fine-grained subscriptions, Redux or Zustand may still be preferable.

items.question: Do all consumers re-render when context changes?
items.answer: Yes, by default. All components using useContext re-render when the Provider value changes. Split contexts to minimize re-renders.

items.question: Can I update context from a consumer?
items.answer: Yes. Pass both the value and an updater function in the context value object, or use useState inside the Provider.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Context eliminates prop drilling by broadcasting data to descendants.
Create with createContext, provide with Provider, consume with useContext.
Use context for truly global data, not for component-local sharing.
Split contexts by concern to avoid unnecessary re-renders.
data.takeaway: Context is a powerful tool for escaping prop drilling. Next, you will master the useContext hook.
